summary.text: A 37 year old man with no known comorbidities presented to the emergency department with an alleged history of an accidental cut injury over the right clavicular region from a wood cutting machine. He was hemodynamically stable, with a respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation of 98% in room air, and had an approximately 8x6 cm open wound with exposed clavicular bone.

The wound was washed and tetanus toxoid was given. Chest and clavicle radiographs revealed a midshaft right clavicle fracture, classified as Gustilo Anderson grade II and Robinson 2B1. Total blood count and inflammatory markers were within normal limit.

The wound was debrided and left open with sterile dressing, and he was admitted on prophylactic IV cefuroxime, metronidazole and amikacin. With the wound healthy and no culture taken, definitive fixation with an 8 hole anatomical locking plate with screws was done on day four, followed by sling immobilization and physiotherapy.

Sutures were removed on the 14th post-operative day without wound related complications, antibiotics were discontinued after two weeks, and follow-up until the sixth week showed no signs of infection. The post operative X-ray showed the implant in situ with no displacement, and a Constant-Murley Shoulder outcome Score of 59 was reported as a good clinical outcome.
